title: ItemEvent
description: A dated change in an item's situation: it appeared, was placed, became unattended, moved, was picked up, or was seen being carried while worn. Events are the units the chat cites and links to. ItemEvent deliberately cannot express a staff handover — that requires an intake record and lives in a separate collection, so no pipeline output can accidentally claim a handover.

event_id.description: Stable, content-derived identifier. The same physical event reprocessed in an overlapping window must yield the same event_id so retries cannot duplicate it.

event_type.description: first_observed = earliest sighting in available footage (NOT proof the item arrived then). unattended_onset_estimated = the estimate, which may be marked uncertain. unattended_confirmed = the system's threshold crossing, which lags the onset. worn_seen = the item was on a person and is not a candidate for loss.

event_time_offset_s.description: Media-relative offset of the event. This is what playback seeks to.

event_time.description: Absolute UTC instant, when the source has a wall-clock anchor. Null otherwise; the chat then reports an offset, not an invented clock time.

window_id.description: The 10-minute report window this event was recorded in. Required so every event resolves to a report.

report_id.description: The grouped report (hourly by default) that contained the window at write time. Informational; the window_id is authoritative.

onset_certainty.description: Repeated here so a single event can be scored without loading its observation. 'uncertain' is required when the item was already present at clip start.

uncertainty.description: Uncertainty inherited from the observation plus anything specific to this event.

evidence_id.description: Reference to the evidence record for this event. Required: an event with no evidence cannot be cited in an answer.

is_worn.description: Inherited from the observation. True events of type worn_seen are never loss candidates.

note.description: Short factual context for the answer, e.g. 'a person sat down, then left'. Must not state ownership or identity.
